messages.name: bassenhancement
messages.digest: The wordfollowed by a non-zero number will enable the specialized enhancement of low frequencies by the multiband compressor; followed by 0, causes no low frequency enhancement to be applied
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a non-zero number will enable the specialized enhancement of low frequencies by the multiband compressor; followed by 0, causes no low frequency enhancement to be applied.

messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the amount of low-frequency enhancement added into the audio signal before output.

messages.name: bypass
messages.digest: Bypass processing and output the unprocessed signal
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a non-zero number will output the dry unchanged input signal straight out the outlet without any processing; followed by a 0, will output the signal effected by.

messages.name: choosePreset
messages.digest: Select a preset
messages.description: The word, followed by a number in the range 0-2, selects a preset for theobject. These presets are to be considered "starting points" and should be tweaked for your particular purpose or desired sound. The preset options are:0: Universal - Provides a general boost to the sound, with a 3-to-1 compression and no limiting. Bass enhancement is switched in for a bit of warmth.1; Pop - Sets a 50:1 compression with hard driven limiting in the lowest two bands. The gives a solid bottom to the sound.2: Hit Radio - Is a compromise between the Universal and Pop settings. You will note that the times are all about the same, with appropriately slower attack and release in the low bands.3: FM Radio - Differs from the Pop and Hit radio settings primarily in the high end, which is compressed a bit tighter.

messages.name: freeze_threshold
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets the freeze threshold (in dB below full scale). When the input signal drops below the freeze threshold, release will seize completely. Along with the gating threshold, this threshold is useful to prevent background hiss amplification
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the freeze threshold (in dB below full scale). When the input signal drops below the freeze threshold, release will seize completely. Along with the gating threshold, this threshold is useful to prevent background hiss amplification.

messages.name: gating_threshold
messages.digest: Set the release gate threshold
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the release gate threshold (in dB below full scale). When the signal is below this threshold, the release time of the compressor will be slowed by a factor of 3.

messages.name: inagc_atk
messages.digest: Set the attack rate for the input compressor
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the attack rate for the input compressor. The attack rate determines how quickly the compressor applies gain reduction. The value range is 0-150 on a logarithmic scale, with larger values indicating faster attack.

messages.name: inagc_progressive
messages.digest: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables the Progressive Release mode, which causes the input compressor to release faster during heavy gain reduction
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables the Progressive Release mode, which causes the input compressor to release faster during heavy gain reduction.

messages.name: inagc_range
messages.digest: Set the maximum gain applied by the input compressor
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the maximum amount of gain in dB applied by the input compressor .

messages.name: inagc_ratio
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio, from 1:1 to Infinite:1
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio, from 1:1 to Infinite:1.

messages.name: inagc_rel
messages.digest: Set the release rate for the input compressor
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the release rate for the input compressor. The release rate determines how quickly the compressor returns to unity gain. The value range is 0-150 on a logarithmic scale, with larger values indicating faster release.

messages.name: inagc_threshold
messages.digest: The word inagc_threshold, followed by a number, sets the compression threshold level (in dB below full scale)
messages.description: The word inagc_threshold, followed by a number, sets the compression threshold level (in dB below full scale) for the input compressor.

messages.name: inf_ratio_above_threshold_1
messages.digest: The word, followed by a zero or one, disables/enables Infinite ratio above threshold (sometimes called "soft clipping") for band 1. If enabled, the ratio in that band will be Infinite:1 any time there is gain reduction (i.e. the input signal is above the threshold), no matter what the Multiband Ratio is set to

messages.name: lim_drive
messages.digest: Set the overall gain before peak limiting is applied
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the overall gain in dB before peak limiting is applied.

messages.name: lim_smoothrelease
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets the limiter response mode as follows:0: Punchy. Punchy response yields extremely short attack and release times, useful for transparent limiting, or to create loudness. However, if over-used, intermodulation distortion may result.1: Smooth. Smooth release uses longer attack and release times. The result is still a fast look-ahead limiter, but with less intermodulation distortion and less punch
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the limiter response mode as follows:0: Punchy. Smooth release uses longer attack and release times. The result is still a fast look-ahead limiter, but with less intermodulation distortion and less punch.

messages.name: mbrange
messages.digest: Set the maximum gain applied by the multiband compressor
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the maximum amount of gain in dB applied by the multiband compressor. This limits the gain that is applied when the signal is below the compression threshold. Note that this limiting takes place before the ratio is applied. For example, if the range is set to 24 dB, and the ratio is 2:1, the most gain amplification you can get (after the ratio is applied) is in fact 12 dB.

messages.name: mbratio
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio, from 1:1 to Infinite:1
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the numerator of the compressor gain reduction ratio, from 1:1 to Infinite:1.

messages.name: meterData
messages.digest: Output internal state value data
messages.description: The wordwill cause output (by instantaneous command as opposed to metering-interval described by themessage) of values which describe the current state of various internal levels of the compressor, and can be used to drive GUI objects to provide visual feedback.

messages.name: meterRate
messages.digest: Set the metering output interval
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, specifies the interval (in milliseconds) at which the meter data described above will be sent.

messages.name: meters
messages.digest: Disable/enable the metering output
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, turns the metering output on or off. When metering is on, a list of values will be sent from the rightmost outlet at a rate specified by themessage. These values describe the current state of various internal levels of the compressor, and can be used to drive GUI objects to provide visual feedback.

messages.name: multiband_limiters
messages.digest: Disable/enable the peak limiting
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables the peak limiting function, which limits the signal level of each frequency band independently, so it does not exceed the threshold set for that band.

messages.name: ng_enabled_maxch
messages.digest: Disable/enable the noise gating for the multiband compressor
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, enables or disables noise gating for the multi-band compressor. The noise gating itself has multiple bands, separate from the compressor, allowing independent control via themessages.

messages.name: ngenabled
messages.digest: Disable/enable the noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 0, turns the noise gate on or off. A noise gate is effective for reducing background hiss when no other signal is present.features two noise gates: one that operates on the entire signal, and one that only affects higher frequencies, such as hiss.

messages.name: ngthresh1
messages.digest: Set the threshold level for the band 1 noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that specifies a threshold level (expressed as dB below full scale), sets the threshold level at which the noise gate for band 1 will be engaged.

messages.name: ngthresh2
messages.digest: Set the threshold level for the band 2 noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that specifies a threshold level (expressed as dB below full scale), sets the threshold level at which the noise gate for band 2 will be engaged.

messages.name: ngthresh3
messages.digest: Set the threshold level for the band 3 noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that specifies a threshold level (expressed as dB below full scale), sets the threshold level at which the noise gate for band 3 will be engaged.

messages.name: ngthresh4
messages.digest: Set the threshold level for the band 4 noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that specifies a threshold level (expressed as dB below full scale), sets the threshold level at which the noise gate for band 4 will be engaged.

messages.name: ngthresh5
messages.digest: Set the threshold level for the band 5 noise gate
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that specifies a threshold level (expressed as dB below full scale), sets the threshold level at which the noise gate for band 5 will be engaged.

messages.name: outlevel_lf
messages.digest: Set the left channel output level
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the left channel output level in dB for theobject.

messages.name: outlevel_rf
messages.digest: Set the right channel output level
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the right channel output level in dB for theobject.

messages.name: outmix1
messages.digest: Set the post-compression gain for band 1
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the gain in dB applied to band 1 after compression.

messages.name: outmix2

messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the gain in dB applied to band 2 after compression.

messages.name: outmix3

messages.name: outmix4

messages.name: outmix5

messages.name: output_level
messages.digest: Set the output level
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the output level. This setting is used for attenuating the output, but clipping will never occur even if you set it to gain. The gain for each channel will take both this control and the controls on the Global Settings page into account, but the gain for each channel will be clamped below 0 to prevent clipping.

messages.name: saveSettings
messages.digest: Send all parameter values out the third outlet
messages.description: The wordcauses all parameter values to be sent out the third outlet.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Audio input
messages.description: Audio input, the signal or pair of signals to be compressed.

messages.name: spatial_desired
messages.digest: Adjust the spatial enhancer
messages.description: The spatial enhancer separates the channels of mixes that are nearly (but not quite) mono by subtracting a bit of left from the right signal and vice versa, but only when the two are nearly the same. The word, followed by a number, sets the difference between the side signal and the combined (mono) signal,

messages.name: spatial_enabled
messages.digest: Disable/enable spatial enhancement
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, disables/enables spatial enhancement.

messages.name: spatial_maximum
messages.digest: Set the maximum gain on signals used for spatial enhancement
messages.description: The spatial enhancer separates the channels of mixes that are nearly (but not quite) mono by subtracting a bit of left from the right signal and vice versa, but only when the two are nearly the same. The word, followed by a number, sets the maximum gain on the two difference signals.

messages.name: spatial_speed
messages.digest: Set the speed of response to changes in separation
messages.description: The spatial enhancer separates the channels of mixes that are nearly (but not quite) mono by subtracting a bit of left from the right signal and vice versa, but only when the two are nearly the same. The word, followed by a number, sets the speed of response to changes in separation.
